outline.purpose: Trace request, helper, schema, component, and persistence ownership only through packages/web/src/app/api/skills/route.ts:publishSkillSchema and POST safeParse; packages/shared/src/schemas/skill-schema.ts:shared skill validation. outline.heading: Step-by-Step Publish request issue array Procedure
outline.purpose: Present the numbered procedure for publish request issue array: Derive boundary fixtures from publishSkillSchema and the shared skill schema. POST each fixture and capture status, top-level error, and ordered issue details. Assert invalid payloads never query users, slugs, or inserts. Compare route validation with shared SKILL.md validation to document intentional differences.

outline.heading: Nextjs post schema testing: Assertions and Diagnostics
outline.purpose: Cover nextjs post schema testing with status, state, side-effect, call-count, and visible-output assertions. Explain the failure signal a CI report must retain.

outline.heading: What Regressions and Boundaries Prevent False Confidence?
outline.purpose: Do not claim the route and shared schemas are identical; the article must expose overlaps and intentional transport-specific fields. List nearby concerns owned by related articles and define the post-change cases that remain in scope.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.purpose: Answer five to eight questions in 40 to 60 words each. Cover "How do you test every publish field boundary and verify the combined error message plus structured Zod issue array?" plus question variants based on zod api error response test, skill description length validation, github url validation test, publish request issue array, nextjs post schema testing.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.purpose: Summarize the verified contract without introducing new claims, then use this CTA: Open the skill publishing guide and add every schema boundary to the API validation regression matrix.
